source_changes.required_tests_per_job: Integration.account proved the committed integration settlement against `self.required_tests()` with NO Job id. That overload selects 'the one implementation worker' and refuses a deployment configuring several, so the terminal completion check of EITHER Job would have failed under a /2 document. It now passes this stage's own bound Job id, the same `_bound_id` the two operand lines above it use.
source_changes.integration_runtime_port_per_job: `IntegrationRuntimePort` is composed over ONE accepted line, ONE published proposal and ONE canonical target, and all three are per-Job facts. `operations_from(integration_port=)` now accepts a MAPPING of bound Job id to port; `_integration_ports` keeps the single-object spelling for one binding and REFUSES one bare port for a deployment binding several rather than running a second Job's integration against the first Job's line. `Integration.port_for` selects by the stage's own Job, and the /1 binding answers for every Job it is asked about exactly as `binding_for` does.
source_changes.derived_integration_task: `_served_deployment` now derives `task_document` and `task_bytes` alongside `input_manifest` from the bound producer, because `_held` proves the configured task document's bytes against the manifest's own human contract and a half-derived document would be one that validator would never have accepted.
source_changes.no_new_capability: no new provider, driver, profile, actor or grant. The port is the same accepted object, supplied once per Job by the same operator that supplies one today.

fixture_changes.per_job_task_document: the shared two-Job fixture now gives Job B its own task document declaring its own line's base. Without it Job B's producer could never run a turn at all: the workload plans its checkout from `declared_base` and refuses a base its mounted line has never heard of. `bound_worker` moves a worker's manifest and its task document together, because `_held` refuses the pair when they disagree.
fixture_changes.second_job_routes: `EachJobBindsItsOwnDeploymentAndLine` now declares the second producer's and second reviewer's routes on the Authority, exactly as `ServingCase` already declares the first Job's. A fenced handoff moves the Work onto the route the next role is served on, and a participant the Authority does not know serves that route has its claim refused there.
fixture_changes.concurrent_engine: `_ConcurrentEngine` models SEVERAL live containers. The accepted `test_single_worker.Engine` models exactly one -- `runtime_id`, `image`, `labels` and `mounts` are single-valued and `inspect` answers about the last container started whatever identity it was asked about -- so two Jobs coding at once reported each other's runtime and the second producer's stage projected `exceptional` the instant the first one started. The accepted Engine is NOT changed; the cases that own it start one container at a time.
fixture_changes.one_canonical_target: the traversal binds its two Jobs to two lines of ONE canonical target at that target's own revision. `integration.driver` refuses a proposal built on any other revision -- 'a proposal is offered against the revision it was built from' -- and an Authority holds one. `two_jobs()` itself is untouched, so the admission fixture and every accepted case over it are exactly as accepted.
